question: Should OpenClaw accept this private aggregate recovery-point contract now, including the runtime-state owner's selected-agent inventory boundary and the ownership of portability obligations, before any integrated capture caller exists?
rationale: The decision establishes a cross-owner persistent recovery identity and determines whether an intentionally uncalled core contract is an acceptable first slice; code review cannot safely choose that product and ownership boundary.

options.title: Defer pending RFC owner acceptance
options.body: Keep the PR open until snapshot and runtime-state owners accept the inventory and obligation boundaries in the linked RFC, then refresh proof against the accepted contract.

options.title: Accept the bounded private contract
options.body: Approve this as a deliberately private foundation, with follow-up capture and restore PRs required to retain the exact accepted manifest semantics.

options.title: Request an integrated first slice
options.body: Ask for the manifest to land only with its concrete capture owner so the format is not introduced as an unused standalone core contract.

recommendation.title: Defer pending RFC owner acceptance
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until snapshot and runtime-state owners accept the inventory and obligation boundaries in the linked RFC, then refresh proof against the accepted contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the proposed contract and linked RFC stack, although the required snapshot/runtime-owner approval should be supplied by the responsible owners rather than inferred from authorship.
